title: Broken: an incremental load that misses late rows
objective_text: Diagnose why an incremental load never picks up rows that arrive late, repair the filter and the watermark, and prove the repaired job is safe to run twice.
scenario: Finance says order 1006 is in the source system but not in the lakehouse, and the load job reports success every night. The job is the SQL in your workspace: it was copied from a tutorial and has run unchanged for months.
verifies: Your repaired job ran twice on this PC with DuckDB; silver_orders got every missing order exactly once and load_state holds the right watermark.
Nothing outside silver_orders and load_state changed.
does_not_verify: The same job as a Fabric pipeline or notebook, where the watermark is usually stored in a table or a pipeline variable.
Source systems whose arrival timestamps can go backwards, which need an overlap window.

fault.summary: The job filters on the business date (order_date) instead of the arrival time, and stores a date-only watermark taken from order_date.

planted.what: order_date > watermark: a row with an old order_date that arrives late is never selected
the watermark is max(order_date) as a date, so it doesn't follow arrivals and loses the time of day
the stored watermark (2 April 00:00) is earlier than rows already loaded, so a repaired filter alone would load 1003 and 1004 again

fault.symptom: Order 1006 (ordered 1 April, arrived 3 April) is in source_orders but never reaches silver_orders.

expected.result: The starter's final SELECT over silver_orders and load_state.

validation.pass: Every order is loaded once and the watermark is the last arrival.
validation.fail: Compare silver_orders with source_orders, then look at the watermark after the second run.

validation.pass: Running the job twice didn't duplicate anything.
validation.fail: An order is in silver_orders twice: the second run loaded it again.
The job changed source_orders; a load only reads its source.

hints: Find 1006 in source_orders. Which of its two dates is after the watermark, and which one does the job compare?
An incremental load should select by when a row arrived (arrived_at), not by what the row is about (order_date).
Before the first repaired run, repair the state too: the stored watermark is earlier than rows already in silver_orders. Set it to max(arrived_at) of silver_orders.
Store the new watermark as max(arrived_at) of what's loaded, as a timestamp, and compare with > so the second run selects nothing.
explanation: A watermark must use a column that only grows as rows arrive: an arrival or modified timestamp, or a source sequence number. A business date such as order_date can be in the past for a row that arrives today, so a filter on it skips late rows forever while the job keeps succeeding. The watermark must also be stored at full precision and advanced to the largest value actually loaded; with > (not >=) the next run starts exactly after it, so the job is safe to repeat. Repairing a broken incremental job means repairing its state as well as its code: a watermark written by the broken version can point before rows already loaded.
reset: Reset restores source_orders, silver_orders, load_state and the original load_orders.sql.
